newsitem.title: UK: Event risk fears jolt buyers into Woolwich bond.
newsitem.headline: Event risk fears jolt buyers into Woolwich bond.

text.p: Event risk associated with British utilities is causing investors to switch into debt issued by financial institutions, dealers said on Friday.
"There is increasing concern about the event risk associated with some corporates and utilities following recent shake-ups in the sector," a syndicate manager at CS First Boston said.
The securities house has made a strong argument to its clients that they should be switch from corporate into financial paper.
British utility bond volatility reflects concerns about further regulatory shake-ups and take-over bids in the sector.
"Event risk" is the risk a borrower's credit rating may fall due to regulatory changes, takeovers or corporate restructuring.

Today's strong demand for Woolwich Building Society's bond -- a 150 million stg subordinated perpetual bond -- via joint lead managers CS First Boston and HSBC Markets, appeared to show investors felt safer putting their money into financial paper.

"There's also been strong demand in the long end of the sterling market which is pushing spreads in and leaving investors looking for paper due to lack of supply," the CS First Boston syndicate manager said.
"And based on this we were able to do this deal and place it with British institutions," he added.
Also the positive credit outlook for building societies converting into banks had helped to boost the Woolwich bond, he said.
Woolwich -- whose subordinated debt is rated A3 by Moody's -- intends to demutualize and become a bank in 1997.
The bond was priced to yield 125 basis points over the 8.0 percent gilt due 2021 and pays a 9.25 percent coupon -- said to be the highest yielding perpetual in the market.
The bond may be called at par after 25 years and every five years thereafter. If not called, the coupon will be reset to yield 225 b.p. over the prevailing five-year gilt.
Some traders said the perpetual was issued too soon after a 200 million stg 25-year bond it launched in July.
That bond was priced to yield 115 b.p. over the 8.0 percent gilt due 2021 via BZW and UBS. Traders said the bond was trading at around 111/112 b.p. over gilts on Friday.
